ProjectWeave request for the selected Task (data):
{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjccM8AAAABZhWBEg", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3IfzhDIVrs", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3If", "number": 57, "title": "Correct V30MZ AAA/AAS results, flags and execution clocks", "body": "## Problem

At baseline `31862d19b85da3204b2afa90bee04b7d070625cc`, `crates/ws-core/src/cpu.rs:753–769` adjusts the whole AX by `0106`, masks AL afterward, updates only AF/CF and retains the default one-clock execution component. This can incorrectly change AH twice and preserve incorrect arithmetic flags, affecting subsequent arithmetic and branches. Commercial-title impact remains unmeasured.

Static reproductions, not executed during planning:

| Instruction | Input AX / FLAGS | Current AX / FLAGS | Expected AX / FLAGS |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AAA | `00FA / F002` | `0200 / F013` | `0100 / F057` |
| AAS | `0100 / F012` | `FF0A / F013` | `000A / F057` |
| AAA or AAS | `AB00 / F002` | `AB00 / F002` | `AB00 / F086` |

The existing decimal-conversion smoke test asserts ordinary AX results without checking complete AAA/AAS flags or these boundary cases.

## Expected outcome

Implement AAA (`37`) and AAS (`3F`) using the evidenced V30MZ behavior: determine adjustment from incoming AF or the original low nibble exceeding nine; mask AL before adjustment; adjust AL and AH independently; finally retain only AL's low nibble. AH increments for adjusted AAA and decrements for adjusted AAS, wrapping as a byte.

For both instructions, PF is set and OF cleared; AF/CF/ZF equal the adjustment condition, and SF is its inverse. Preserve control/fixed flag bits and unrelated state. These flags must not be calculated as ordinary result SZP.

Use nine execution clocks plus the repository's existing fetch/wait accounting. Apply the correction across emulated Mono/Color/SwanCrystal model configurations. Keep production scope to these instructions and necessary cross-file tests, original fixtures, browser coverage and documentation. DAA/DAS, exceptional division and prefetch redesign remain separate work.

## Context

The clean local checkout and inspected remote main match the baseline. The open Issue/PR collection is empty; all 56 closed-work titles were checked without finding equivalent completed work. Issue #55 and PR #56 address AAM/AAD separately.

The pinned [WSCPUTest report](https://github.com/FluBBaOfWard/WSCPUTest/blob/245b12c06dede4a2bb9c04c942ebca2044ba4930/README.md#aaa--adjba) describes AAA/AAS flags. Its [AAA calculator and comparisons](https://github.com/FluBBaOfWard/WSCPUTest/blob/245b12c06dede4a2bb9c04c942ebca2044ba4930/WSCpuTest.asm#L6407) and [AAS calculator](https://github.com/FluBBaOfWard/WSCPUTest/blob/245b12c06dede4a2bb9c04c942ebca2044ba4930/WSCpuTest.asm#L6641) establish separate byte adjustment and complete expected flags. The experiment constants include incoming IF; preserve emulator control bits instead of copying those constants unconditionally. These sources were inspected without executing them or inspecting independent per-model silicon logs. Applicability across graphics modes is an instruction-level inference.

The [NEC V30MZ manual](https://www.renesas.com/en/document/lbr/v30mztm-hardware-preliminary), Appendix A, Table A-1, lists nine clocks for ADJBA/ADJBS after decoding under its stated conditions. Adding current fetch charges is the repository's bounded timing policy, not a claim of exact pipeline timing.

Correction record: replace the whole-word-adjust, AF/CF-only and default-cost assumptions with the requirements above, recording sources and rationale. Evidence-based corrections to AI-authored requirements need neither human approval nor independent AI re-review; preserve the agreed goal and relevant acceptance.

[Saved #55 validation](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/31862d19b85da3204b2afa90bee04b7d070625cc/docs/issue-55-validation.md) reports 153 core unit tests, 30 integration tests, one adapter test and complete production Chromium suites passing. These are saved reports, not planning-time executions. Browser evidence precedes its final fixture-input adjustment, and the record still requests final Coordinator review. It does not establish AAA/AAS correctness or commercial compatibility.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Correct both instructions through ordinary decoding. Assert one-byte consumption, continuation, independent AH wrapping, complete FLAGS and unchanged unrelated registers, segments, memory, ports and saves. Preserve existing prefix and interrupt behavior.
- [ ] Add independent literal AX/full-FLAGS cases for every reproduction above, adjusted nonzero AL, unadjusted zero AL and AH wrap boundaries. Supplement them with automated coverage of all 256 incoming AL values, both AF states and AH values `00,01,FE,FF`, using contrasting incoming arithmetic/control flags. Expected values must come from documented independent tables or vectors, without production adjustment/ALU helpers. Exercise flag-dependent branches, including constant PF/cleared OF and ZF/SF independent of result zero/sign.
- [ ] Cover all nine supported static model/mode combinations and Color/Crystal runtime round trips `00→80→00→C0→00→E0→00`. Test RAM and mapped-ROM fetches with waits enabled/disabled. Assert a nine-clock execution component plus actual existing fetch charges: unprefixed RAM/fast-ROM totals ten clocks and waited-ROM totals eleven. Verify normal Machine scheduling applies returned clocks once with timer/raster/PCM observations; preserve existing DMA accounting and unrelated timing acceptance.
- [ ] Add or extend an original source-included CC0 probe using `fixtures/build.py` and NASM. Native and production Chromium/Wasm checks must compare actual CPU-written AX, full FLAGS and branch observations against independent literals on every model, supported runtime transitions and fresh restart. Clear volatile observations and invalidate poisoned retained success records. Record focused native and cartridge failures against the old handlers, configurations reached, and corrected passes.
- [ ] Before merge, the Coordinator passes `python3 fixtures/build.py --check`, `python3 demo/build.py --check`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo test --workspace --locked`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, and `git diff --check`. In `web`, pass `npm run build:wasm`, `npm run build`, then complete `npm run test:browser` and `npm run test:compat` sequentially against a locally served production preview. Validate the final fixture/test revisions; record which revision each result covers.
- [ ] Preserve prior AAM/AAD, multiplication, division, shift/rotate, PUSH SP, BUSLOCK and interrupt regressions, plus existing three-model startup/firmware, video/input/frame, audio/PCM, GDMA/SDMA/Hyper Voice, RTC transport, SRAM/EEPROM and Wasm/browser lifecycle/save-integrity acceptance. Preserve ROM identity, browser-local ownership and provenance policies; require no proprietary ROM or firmware.
- [ ] Update `docs/hardware-subset.md`, source reconciliation and fixture/provenance documentation. Record actual commands, failures, resolutions, passes and unperformed checks. The Coordinator reviews the final diff against every checkbox before merge, distinguishing tests present from execution evidence and retaining explicit hardware/commercial uncertainties.

## Optional validation

Baseline production-browser discrimination, additional browser engines and additional lawfully available software. Physical-console measurements and human gameplay are optional evidence, unperformed during planning, and never merge prerequisites. No files were changed, agents spawned, remote mutations made, or application builds/tests run during planning.

## Required post-merge verification

None

## Specification reconciliation

This task was authored by AI under the agreed WonderSwan-family hardware goal.
Correct erroneous technical assumptions or acceptance criteria when primary hardware
specifications establish the correction. Update this Issue and record the original
assumption, corrected requirement, primary reference and rationale in the PR.
These technical corrections require neither human approval nor an independent AI
re-review. Preserve the agreed goal and relevant pre-merge acceptance; do not weaken
requirements merely to accommodate incomplete implementation or failing tests.

This autonomous campaign has no human-approval gate. Mandatory acceptance uses
automated native and production-browser tests on the emulator's supported model
and mode configurations. Physical-console measurements and human gameplay are
optional evidence and must remain explicitly unperformed unless actually available.
Do not invent device identities, real-device results or a requirement for human
confirmation. Resolve technical errors with recorded evidence and automated checks
through the existing Coordinator workflow.
